what_its_for: Trihexyphenidyl is used to treat symptoms of Parkinson's disease, such as muscle stiffness, tremors (shaking), and slow movement. It is also used to treat movement problems caused by certain psychiatric medications. It works by blocking a chemical in the brain called acetylcholine, which helps your muscles move more smoothly.
how_to_take: Take trihexyphenidyl by mouth exactly as your doctor prescribes. You can take it with or without food, but if it upsets your stomach, taking it with meals may help. If you take it as a liquid, use the measuring device that comes with the medicine — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as stopping too quickly can make your symptoms worse.
dosing: Your doctor will usually start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over time. The typical starting dose is 1 mg once a day. Your doctor may increase your dose by 2 mg every 3 to 5 days until your symptoms are well controlled. Most people end up taking 6 to 10 mg per day, divided into 3 doses taken throughout the day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store trihexyphenidyl at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the liquid form tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing activities that require you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid getting overheated or dehydrated — this medicine can reduce sweating, which makes it harder for your body to cool down. Be careful in hot weather or during exercise. Avoid taking antacids, stomach medicines, or other anticholinergic medicines (such as certain allergy, bladder, or stomach medications) without asking your doctor first, as they can increase side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: confusion, hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there), memory problems, extreme drowsiness, fast or irregular heartbeat, difficulty urinating or inability to urinate, severe constipation, blurred vision, eye pain, skin that is very hot and dry with no sweating, high fever, or swelling of the hands, feet, or ankles. Also call your doctor if you feel your symptoms are getting worse or if you notice any new or unusual symptoms.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your muscle stiffness and tremors within a few days of starting trihexyphenidyl. However, it may take several weeks of dose adjustments before you get the full benefit of this medicine. Be patient and keep taking it as directed, even if you do not feel better right away.
special_populations: Older adults (over 65): This medicine should be used with extra caution in older adults because they are more likely to experience serious side effects such as confusion, memory problems, hallucinations, and falls. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as safety has not been fully established. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Certain health conditions: Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma (high eye pressure), an enlarged prostate, difficulty urinating, severe constipation, or heart problems, as this medicine may make those conditions worse.
